utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. Mark Harmon, Bronagh McKenna, and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning to all. Jason Keck and Gregor Guy-Smith on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Sir, just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. I hope you had a good rest last night. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam McKenna.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honour, having reviewed the record, we have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam McKenna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question to ask. Yesterday, answering a question from the Defence of the accused, you stated that Lieutenant Pelemis, I'm trying to find it, had economic interests or was -- had rather mirky economic interests. And I was wondering whether when he gave you the order to go to the Pilica farm to execute the prisoners who were taken there by buses, was it himself who decided himself to do this or whether he had received orders from above from some superior?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer now? I did not see or hear him receive orders, but judging by what happened that day, the fact that we went to Zvornik and reported to another officer, I think -- in fact, I know that he had received orders and that it was all organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: And these orders, according to you, did they come from the Main Staff -- from the Serbs of Bosnia or any other source?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those orders came down from the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: This was my only question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: You said at page 39, line 15 to 19, you said: "People were taken off the bus, taken to the field, and executed." And also you said: "When they were recognised, they mistreated them ..." Could you elaborate more on the type of mistreatment that those recognised were subjected to?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certain people from my unit as well as from Bratunac who later joined us would recognise some of the individuals from Srebrenica. Some of those individuals were originally from Bratunac and then during the war fled to Srebrenica. These prisoners would be recognised and then they would be singled out, physically mistreated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: What kind of physical mistreatment do you remember or verbal?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was verbal abuse but also physical abuse. They would beat them with soldiers' rifles, kick them, punch them. Also they would beat them with some sort of metal bars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That was my only question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench. Madam McKenna?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I may have one if I could just double-check something very quickly. No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony today. Thank you so much for taking the time to come and testify. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam McKenna -- Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have no additional witnesses for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We then adjourn, adjourn to tomorrow at 9.00, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of July, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.10 a.m.,
